Where it began

Nathan Lyon was born on 20 November 1987 in Young, New South Wales. He moved to Canberra as a teenager and came through the ACT's under-17 and under-18 sides before joining the Comets. Their captain, Mark Higgs, took him under his wing and helped shape his bowling.

In 2010 he moved to Adelaide, where he worked on the ground staff at the Adelaide Oval. A good night with the ball in a Futures League Twenty20 game in Melbourne caught the eye of Darren Berry, South Australia's Twenty20 coach, and he was picked for the Big Bash. He finished that season as its leading wicket-taker, and the Redbacks won the title.

The player

His Test debut came at Galle in August 2011, with his baggy green handed to him by Greg Chappell. With his very first ball in Test cricket he dismissed Kumar Sangakkara, and he went on to take five wickets in the innings.

In 2015 he passed Hugh Trumble as the most successful Australian off-spinner, and in 2017 he took 8 for 50 at Bangalore, the best figures by a visiting bowler in India. He took five wickets as Australia won the World Test Championship final in 2023, and at Lord's in 2023 he became the first specialist bowler to play 100 Tests in a row. By November 2026 he had played 144 Tests and taken 573 wickets at 30.26, with 24 five-wicket innings and five ten-wicket matches. On our figures only five men had taken more.

What made him special

Some of his finest work came in Asia. In Chittagong in 2017 he took 13 for 154, the best match figures by an Australian in Asia, and in 2023 he passed Derek Underwood's record for Test wickets in India by a touring bowler. He was named Australia's Test player of the year in 2019 and again in 2024, and the ICC picked him in its Test side of the year in 2018, 2019 and 2022.

His batting was more of a hobby. A Test average of 12.93 tells its own tale, though his older brother, who coaches his batting, might point out that in 2013–14 he got through an entire five-Test series without being dismissed once.

Away from the middle

During a series against South Africa in 2016, Matthew Wade kept shouting "Nice, Garry" from behind the stumps after his deliveries, a nod to a famous Melbourne footballer of the same surname. The crowds took it up, and Lyon became a cult hero. Fittingly for a man who started out on a ground staff, he became an ambassador for Australian apprenticeships in 2017. Away from cricket he follows the Canberra Raiders in rugby league.

And finally

In a Sheffield Shield match in 2017 he managed to burn his toast in the dressing room, set off the smoke alarm and bring the fire brigade to the ground. Play stopped for 30 minutes. For a man who spent his working life making things turn, it was a rare case of overcooking.
